title: First Project in UE5 with Claude Ultra
author: 999Jupiter999
selftext:
I just want to preface this post by saying I have created a few other projects before with Claude and with other AI agents as well but this was my first time doing a project at all in Unreal Engine 5.

Simply put, the game is obviously a horror game, sort of inspired by the TV show Supernatural and heavily inspired by real folklore stories in the US.

I am on the **Max Subscription**, I have been working on this project for about 2 weeks. With about 2 months of brainstorming and planning before ever starting it, I thought it was just way too big to build but here we are. I am doing it completely solo with just this Max account + Tripo for some of the models. Total Cost in API so far is about $4900, obviously I haven't paid that out of pocket.

There are still of course many glitches and things that need perfecting, but the goal is to have a playable first mission (Wendigo) by January '27. Eventually if we get to a full release, the game is planned to be a Solo OR a Dup experience. **Track & Hunt "Cryptid and Supernatural Entities" in C.A.S.E , for PC.**

Please let me know your thoughts/questions if any, would you or a friend play this?

comments.author: DraconicBlade
comments.body:
Your opener has the same tree model right next to itself center frame in scene 2, also repeating tree models right frame.

Immediately writing it off. Reusing assets in the same shot in under ten seconds. You have told me im being sold leftover casserole breakfast lunch and dinner.

replies.author: imlo2
replies.body:
You do realize that most games re-use tree assets etc. very heavily. Very rarely is real dynamic generation used in any games. They are just instanced with rotation and scaling, and there might not often be more than a handful of variants of one tree type or a rock or such. Otherwise you lose easily benefits of instanced drawing, batching etc. This applies to all the big AAA games etc. What is unfortunate if anything that two trees in same rotation and scale are seen side by side.   
  
But I wouldn't start to call the project being something like leftover food because of that. Would you say that face to face in a review session at a game studio?

replies.author: DraconicBlade
replies.body:
I do realize that. When its slammed in my face immediately, I also realize there's oversight. Lack of care, inattention to detail.

So, I'm gonna assume that note carries through the entire piece.

comments.author: ElderZombie250
comments.body:
How does it all get put together?   If I understand correctly, you're using Tripo (which looks pretty cool btw) to make the models, but how do you get Claude to actually build a scene?   

Sorry for the noob question, but I've only used Claude to work on my code, not to actually build things in my game.  Indeed, when I asked it about performing tasks in Unity, it mostly says it can't really perform action in the editor itself.

Very new to AI game dev, so forgive my ignorance.

replies.author: 999Jupiter999
replies.body:
Thank you I appreciate the comment. Yes I'm using Tripo for the models, and the skeleton mapping (Rigging) allows you to create movements for that character. Rigging it yourself can be tedious and the auto rig doesn't always work great in Tripo. SO, I opened Tripo on my account inside of Claude's in app browser on PC, told an agent to prompt, review, refine, and Rig, for the models I needed movement on.

Everything that Tripo handed back, if it was good to go Claude would do the download through that same in app browser for all of the file types it needs, imported it into unreal engine and got it working from there. If it needed more work after Tripo, like for the Wendigo, that originally had no blood on its model, was able to be taken in its current state and further worked on inside of Blender, by Claude. 

Claudes visual review and refine process is incredibly good if using High/Extra intelligence. I also always ask it to send me photos as it's working if the window it's working in is not visible the whole time, this helps me to catch small mistakes and make refinements before delivering the entire project happens. 

I'm not sure if I answered your question or not, hopefully, if you have any other questions feel free to send me a message or leave a comment here.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
Don't let some of these assholes bother you. 2 weeks may be a bit early but don't listen to naysayers, just keep doing you and making your game. I have been shocked at some of the jerks here. This is supposed to be 
>Exploring "generative AI" technologies to empower game devs and benefit humanity.

Not sale ready only posts. Keep on making.

replies.author: 999Jupiter999
replies.body:
Thank you 🤘 I definitely won't let em get to me. I'm making the game because I feel like the horror games I've played have been underwhelming. I don't know if its even possible to build it at the scale I want yet, but each model keeps getting better and so do my workflows. 

Deep down I'm just a huge fan of all things supernatural (the show and real world) and I felt like a Hunting/Clue Based game with real Folklore could be a fun twist. Still scary like other horror games but with an actual progression system and a world to explore. It's based in the Appalachian mountains, so, many hillside towns and settlements, buildings and houses have purposes, coal mines, train, etc. 

Super super early right now of course. Just happy to be sharing some of my ideas with the world.
